# Voxel and Grid Representations

Also called: Explicit Radiance Fields, Voxel-based NeRF, Grid-based Neural Fields

## Overview
Voxel and Grid Representations replace coordinate-based Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLPs) with explicit, differentiable 3D grids (dense or sparse) to store density and appearance features, enabling faster optimization and rendering [S1]. Unlike MLPs which suffer from slow convergence and limited capacity for high-frequency details, grid-based methods leverage spatial locality and efficient interpolation, allowing for high-fidelity reconstruction at significantly reduced training times [S1].

## Shared principles
The core mechanism involves discretizing the 3D scene space into a grid structure where each voxel (or cell) stores learnable parameters.

**Data Structures:**
*   **Density Grid ($G_\sigma$):** A tensor storing volume density $\sigma$. For a dense grid, this is $\mathbb{R}^{I \times J \times K}$ [S1].
*   **Appearance/Feature Grid ($G_c$ or $G_a$):** A tensor storing latent feature vectors per voxel. Dimensions are $\mathbb{R}^{I \times J \times K \times P}$, where $P$ is the number of feature channels [S1]. These features may include neural embeddings and [spherical harmonics](#5603-spherical-harmonics.md) coefficients [S1].

**Query Mechanism:**
For a query point $p$ in world space, the corresponding grid values are retrieved via interpolation.
1.  Map $p$ to local coordinates within the containing voxel.
2.  Retrieve the 8 corner values from the grid.
3.  Perform trilinear interpolation to obtain the scalar density $\sigma(p)$ and feature vector $f(p)$ [S1].

$$ f(p) = \text{trilinear\_interp}(p, G) $$

This operation is differentiable, allowing gradients to flow back to the grid values during optimization [S1].

**Decoding:**
The retrieved feature vector $f(p)$ and viewing direction $\mathbf{d}$ are typically passed to a small decoding MLP $\mathcal{S}$ to predict color $\mathbf{c}$ [S1].

$$ \mathbf{c} = \mathcal{S}(f(p), \mathbf{d}) $$

**Optimization:**
The grid values are optimized using gradient descent to minimize the difference between rendered images and ground truth. The explicit nature of the grid allows for parallel updates and faster convergence compared to MLP weights [S1].

## Subtopics

### [Adaptive Differentiable Grids for Cryo-ET](17614-adaptive-differentiable-grids-for-cryo-et.md)
[Adaptive Differentiable Grids](#17614-adaptive-differentiable-grids-for-cryo-et.md) (ADG) use an adaptive [octree structure](#2792-octree-based-structures.md) where each enabled node stores a 3D density grid, specifically designed for high-noise cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) reconstruction [17614-adaptive-differentiable-grids-for-cryo-et.md]. Unlike standard neural fields that learn noise, ADG combines differentiable image formation with regularization (Total Variation, Boundary Consistency, Cross-Nodes Non-Local Constraints) to jointly reconstruct and denoise [17614-adaptive-differentiable-grids-for-cryo-et.md]. It is chosen when dealing with low signal-to-noise ratio data where uniform regions must be denoised while preserving detailed features in active nodes [17614-adaptive-differentiable-grids-for-cryo-et.md].

### [Depth-Guided Robust and Fast Point Cloud Fusion NeRF](18135-depth-guided-robust-and-fast-point-cloud-fusion-nerf.md)
This method represents the radiance field as an explicit voxel grid of features constructed via point cloud fusion from sparse RGB-D inputs [18135-depth-guided-robust-and-fast-point-cloud-fusion-nerf.md]. It refines inaccurate depth values by referencing a fused point cloud aggregated from all input views, avoiding error-prone depth completion networks [18135-depth-guided-robust-and-fast-point-cloud-fusion-nerf.md]. It is chosen for novel-view synthesis from sparse inputs where model size and training speed are critical, offering significantly smaller size and faster training than dense voxel or octree variants [18135-depth-guided-robust-and-fast-point-cloud-fusion-nerf.md].

### [Sparse Feature Volume](18180-sparse-feature-volume.md)
The [Sparse Feature Volume](#18180-sparse-feature-volume.md) (SFV) [encodes a scene](#17508-encode-scene.md) as a sparse grid of latent vectors, allocating memory only to occupied regions [18180-sparse-feature-volume.md]. It combines sparse voxel efficiency with neural implicit flexibility, using a coarse-to-fine hierarchy and Transformer-based multi-view feature fusion [18180-sparse-feature-volume.md]. It is chosen for high-fidelity surface reconstruction and online reconstruction, distinguishing itself from dense grids by memory efficiency and from pure MLPs by enabling efficient geometry learning via [SDF-based volume rendering](#9964-sdf-based-volume-rendering.md) [18180-sparse-feature-volume.md].

### Efficient EndoNeRF scene representation
A [voxel-grids-based representation](#2159-voxelgrid.md) that replaces coordinate-based MLPs with explicit density ($\mathbf{V}_\sigma$) and feature volume grids ($\mathbf{V}_a$) to accelerate optimization for dynamic surgical scenes [S1]. It models dynamic scenes by warping a canonical radiance field with a time-dependent deformation field, using decomposed 4D motion fields and a 3-layer MLP to map spatial-temporal coordinates $(\mathbf{x}, t)$ to displacement $\Delta \mathbf{x}$ [S1].

## Background
The shift from coordinate-based MLPs to voxel grids was driven by the need for faster optimization and higher resolution capabilities in [neural radiance fields](#4972-neural-radiance-fields.md) [S1]. Early works like [16–19] (cited in [S1]) demonstrated that implicit-explicit voxel grid representations achieve much faster optimization than pure MLPs. This family of methods has become standard in modern [NeRF](#1185-nerf-neural-radiance-fields.md) variants (e.g., Instant-NGP, [Mip-NeRF 360](#3306-mip-nerf-360.md)) and is widely used in applications requiring real-time rendering or fast training, such as surgical simulation [S1] and cryo-ET [17614-adaptive-differentiable-grids-for-cryo-et.md].
